In [[statistics]], the '''Robbins lemma''', named after [[Herbert Robbins]], states that if ''X'' is a [[random variable]] having a [[Poisson distribution]] with parameter ''&lambda;'', and ''f'' is any function for which the [[expected value]] E(''f''(''X'')) exists, then<ref>{{citation|title=Stochastic Modeling and Mathematical Statistics: A Text for Statisticians and Quantitative Scientists|first=Francisco J.|last=Samaniego|publisher=CRC Press|year=2015|isbn=9781466560475|page=118|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v1HSBQAAQBAJ&pg=PA118}}.</ref>
: <math> \operatorname{E}(X f(X - 1)) = \lambda \operatorname{E}(f(X)). </math>

Robbins introduced this proposition while developing [[empirical Bayes method]]s.
